The count-based tier (Remediation Required) is authoritative per the classification table.

decomposition_strategy.rationale: The service is tiny (2 endpoints, ~45 lines). Full microservice decomposition would be over-engineering. Focus on internal modular structure with clear separation of concerns.

findings.title: Managed Compute — transitioning from EC2 to EKS
findings.description: The service was historically deployed on a single EC2 instance with forever process manager. Containerization artifacts now exist (Dockerfile, K8s manifests) targeting EKS, but no IaC provisions the EKS cluster and the legacy EC2 model is documented as current.
findings.gap: Compute is transitioning from raw EC2 to managed container orchestration but the transition is incomplete — no EKS cluster IaC, no proof of production deployment on managed compute.
findings.recommendation: Complete the EKS migration by provisioning the EKS cluster via Terraform/CDK, deploying the containerized workload, and decommissioning the EC2 instance.

findings.title: Managed Databases — self-managed MongoDB 2.4
findings.description: MongoDB 2.4 is self-managed on an internal IP (10.0.8.20:27017). No RDS, DocumentDB, DynamoDB, or any AWS managed database service found. K8s configmap references mongo-service:27017 — also self-managed.
findings.gap: All database infrastructure is self-managed with no automated backups, failover, patching, or encryption. MongoDB 2.4 is a decade past EOL.
findings.recommendation: Migrate to Amazon DocumentDB (MongoDB-compatible) with Multi-AZ, automated backups, encryption at rest, and IAM authentication. Use AWS DMS for data migration.

findings.title: Workflow Orchestration — business logic inline in handlers
findings.description: No workflow orchestration services present. Business logic (pricing formula) is hardcoded in HTTP handler. Operations are simple (DB read, price calculation) and do not represent multi-step workflows requiring orchestration.
findings.gap: Business logic hardcoded directly in HTTP handler with no structure. Orchestration cannot be layered in if processes grow.
findings.recommendation: Extract business logic into dedicated module. If rate calculations become multi-step, adopt Step Functions.

findings.title: Async Messaging — no messaging infrastructure
findings.description: No messaging or streaming infrastructure exists. The service is entirely synchronous with per-request MongoDB connections. No SQS, SNS, EventBridge, or any async capability.
findings.gap: Complete absence of async capability. Per-request database connection pattern creates latency. No messaging for potential future cross-service communication.
findings.recommendation: Implement connection pooling (upgrade MongoDB driver). If cross-service communication is needed later, adopt SQS/SNS/EventBridge.

findings.title: Network Security — no NetworkPolicy
findings.description: K8s manifests deploy with ClusterIP and hardened securityContext. However, no Kubernetes NetworkPolicy restricts pod-to-pod traffic. Any pod in the cluster can reach this service and MongoDB.
findings.gap: No NetworkPolicy restricts traffic to/from the shipping-rate-api pods. No egress restrictions.
findings.recommendation: Add Kubernetes NetworkPolicy to restrict ingress to authorized consumers and egress to MongoDB only.

findings.title: API Entry Point — no gateway or load balancer
findings.description: No API Gateway, ALB, or CloudFront configured. K8s service exposes directly on ClusterIP. Commented-out ALB Ingress exists but is not active.
findings.gap: Service exposed directly with no gateway or load balancer. No throttling, request validation, or centralized auth at the edge.
findings.recommendation: Deploy AWS ALB Ingress Controller or API Gateway with rate limiting, request validation, and WAF integration.

findings.title: Auto-Scaling — static replicas
findings.description: K8s Deployment has static replicas: 2 with no HPA. Resource requests/limits defined but scaling is entirely static.
findings.gap: No auto-scaling configured. Cannot respond to traffic spikes or scale down during low demand.
findings.recommendation: Add HPA based on CPU/custom metrics. Define minReplicas: 2, maxReplicas: 10 with target CPU at 70%.

findings.title: Backup and Recovery — no backup configuration
findings.description: No backup configuration exists for self-managed MongoDB. No backup plans, no snapshot policies, no mongodump scripts. Data loss would be unrecoverable.
findings.gap: No backup or recovery capability for the database.
findings.recommendation: Migrate to DocumentDB with automated continuous backups and PITR. Interim: implement mongodump to S3.

findings.title: High Availability — single-instance database
findings.description: K8s Deployment with 2 replicas provides compute redundancy. However, MongoDB is single-instance with no replica set or Multi-AZ. Database failure causes total service failure.
findings.gap: Database is single-instance with no failover. No pod anti-affinity to guarantee AZ spread.
findings.recommendation: Migrate to DocumentDB Multi-AZ. Add pod anti-affinity for AZ spread.

findings.title: IaC Coverage — partial, K8s manifests only
findings.description: K8s manifests define deployment topology (Deployment, Service, ConfigMap, Namespace) covering ~20-30% of infrastructure by resource category. No IaC for EKS cluster, VPC, database, monitoring, or secrets management.
findings.gap: Significant infrastructure not in IaC: compute cluster, networking, database, monitoring, operational resources.
findings.recommendation: Adopt Terraform or CDK for full stack: VPC, EKS, DocumentDB, CloudWatch alarms, backup plans. Target 90%+ coverage.

findings.title: CI/CD Automation — no pipeline
findings.description: No CI/CD pipeline definitions. README documents deployment as git pull + forever restart over SSH. CONTAINERIZE.md shows manual kubectl commands.
findings.gap: All deployments fully manual. No automated build, test, security scan, or deploy steps.
findings.recommendation: Implement CI/CD pipeline (CodePipeline+CodeBuild or GitHub Actions) with lint, test, build, push to ECR, deploy to EKS stages.

findings.title: Programming Languages — EOL Node.js and Express
findings.description: Node.js 0.10.x (EOL 2016), Express 3.4.8 (EOL 2015), MongoDB driver 1.4.7 (2014). Compound legacy: language runtime, framework, and driver all end-of-life with known CVEs.
findings.gap: Language runtime, framework, and database driver are all end-of-life. Uses deprecated APIs (express.bodyParser()).
findings.recommendation: Upgrade to Node.js 20 LTS, Express 4.x or Fastify, MongoDB driver 6.x. Refactor callbacks to async/await.

findings.title: Monolith vs Microservices — single-file monolith
findings.description: Entire application is a single file (server.js) with routing, authentication, data access, and business logic interleaved. No module boundaries, no separation of concerns.
findings.gap: Tightly-coupled single-file application with no module boundaries. Cannot scale or maintain components independently.
findings.recommendation: Refactor into modular structure: separate routes, middleware (auth), data access (repository layer), and business logic (pricing). See Decomposition Strategy.

findings.title: Async vs Sync Communication — all synchronous
findings.description: All communication is synchronous. HTTP handlers make callback-based MongoDB calls blocking the request lifecycle. No async messaging or event patterns.
findings.gap: All communication patterns are synchronous with no async capabilities. Per-request MongoDB connections with no pooling.
findings.recommendation: Upgrade MongoDB driver to 6.x with connection pooling. Adopt SQS/SNS for any future inter-service communication.

findings.title: Long-Running Process Handling — all synchronous
findings.description: All operations are synchronous with no timeout protection or async job handling. Per-request MongoDB connections provide no protection against slow queries or network issues.
findings.gap: No async processing capability. No timeout or async fallback exists for database operations.
findings.recommendation: Add request timeouts to MongoDB operations. If operations grow in complexity, implement async job patterns with SQS workers.

findings.title: API Versioning Strategy — no versioning
findings.description: No API versioning. Endpoints are /rates and /quote with no version prefix, no Accept-Version header, no versioning annotations.
findings.gap: No versioning — breaking changes deployed directly to consumers with no migration path.
findings.recommendation: Add URL-based versioning (/v1/rates, /v1/quote). Document versioning contract and deprecation policy.

findings.title: Service Discovery — environment variables via ConfigMap
findings.description: Source code has hardcoded MongoDB IP. K8s deployment externalizes to ConfigMap using K8s DNS-based discovery (mongo-service). No dynamic service discovery.
findings.gap: Environment variables for endpoints but no dynamic discovery. Database endpoint is static.
findings.recommendation: Use AWS Cloud Map or service mesh for dynamic endpoint resolution when migrating to DocumentDB.

findings.title: Unstructured Data Storage — data in self-managed MongoDB
findings.description: All data stored in self-managed MongoDB 2.4. No S3, no object storage, no parsing capabilities.
findings.gap: No managed object storage. Data locked in self-managed MongoDB instance that is EOL and unencrypted.
findings.recommendation: When migrating database, evaluate S3 for rate data exports, archival, or analytics access.

findings.title: Unified Data Access Layer — queries inline in handlers
findings.description: MongoClient.connect() called inside route handlers with inline query construction. No repository pattern, no DAO, no data access abstraction. Unvalidated params passed directly to MongoDB filter (NoSQL injection vector).
findings.gap: Database queries scattered in HTTP handlers with no abstraction. NoSQL injection vulnerability. Testing impossible without live DB.
findings.recommendation: Extract RateRepository module encapsulating all MongoDB operations with input validation and typed interface.

findings.title: Database Engine Version — MongoDB 2.4 EOL since 2016
findings.description: MongoDB 2.4 referenced in README (EOL October 2016). Driver version 1.4.7 targets MongoDB 2.4-2.6. No version pinning in IaC (no database IaC exists).
findings.gap: Database engine is a decade past EOL with known security vulnerabilities and no modern features.
findings.recommendation: Migrate to Amazon DocumentDB (MongoDB 5.0 compatible) with automatic minor version upgrades and automated patching.

findings.title: Encryption at Rest — no encryption
findings.description: No encryption at rest configured. MongoDB 2.4 does not support encryption at rest natively. No KMS keys, no encrypted volumes. Database stores data in plaintext.
findings.gap: Zero encryption at rest. All data stored completely unencrypted on disk with no access control.
findings.recommendation: Migrate to DocumentDB which provides encryption at rest by default using KMS.

findings.title: API Authentication — static shared API key
findings.description: Static API key (ship-2013-abc123-static) checked via x-api-key header. No OAuth2, JWT, or token-based auth. Single shared key for all consumers.
findings.gap: Static API key without per-user identity, rotation, or token-based auth. No audit trail per consumer.
findings.recommendation: Implement JWT/OAuth2 via API Gateway authorizer or Cognito. Each consumer should receive unique credentials.

findings.title: Centralized Identity Integration — no IdP
findings.description: No external identity provider integration. Authentication is entirely self-managed via hardcoded static API key. No Cognito, OIDC, SAML.
findings.gap: Application manages its own authentication with no external IdP, SSO, or federation.
findings.recommendation: Integrate with Amazon Cognito or enterprise IdP for OAuth2/OIDC-based authentication.

findings.title: Secrets Management — plaintext credentials in source
findings.description: Hardcoded API key and MongoDB connection string in server.js committed to git. K8s deployment externalizes to Secret/ConfigMap but application code does not read environment variables.
findings.gap: Critical: plaintext secrets in source code. Credentials exposed in repository history regardless of K8s externalization.
findings.recommendation: Remove hardcoded secrets, read from env vars, rotate compromised key, store in AWS Secrets Manager with rotation, use External Secrets Operator.

findings.title: Compute Hardening — hardened container, no scanning
findings.description: Dockerfile uses node:18-alpine with multi-stage build. K8s enforces non-root, read-only FS, drop ALL caps. But no vulnerability scanning or patching strategy.
findings.gap: Container hardened but no vulnerability scanning or automated patching. EOL dependencies have known CVEs undetected.
findings.recommendation: Add ECR image scanning or Trivy. Implement Dependabot for dependency alerts. Monthly base image rebuilds.

findings.title: Application Security Pipeline — no security scanning
findings.description: No CI/CD pipeline exists, therefore no security scanning integrated. No SAST, DAST, dependency scanning, or container scanning.
findings.gap: No security scanning. Known vulnerabilities in dependencies and application code (NoSQL injection) go undetected.
findings.recommendation: When building CI/CD, include npm audit, Semgrep for SAST, Trivy for container scanning, with gates blocking on critical findings.

findings.title: Distributed Tracing — not instrumented
findings.description: No distributed tracing. No X-Ray, OpenTelemetry, or trace ID propagation. Only console.log for startup.
findings.gap: No tracing capability. Cannot trace requests or identify bottlenecks.
findings.recommendation: Add OpenTelemetry SDK with auto-instrumentation for Express and MongoDB. Enable X-Ray on EKS.

findings.title: SLO Definitions — none defined
findings.description: No SLOs defined. No CloudWatch alarms, no latency targets, no error rate thresholds. No monitoring infrastructure in this repository.
findings.gap: No formal service level definitions. No way to measure service health.
findings.recommendation: Define SLOs: availability 99.9%, p99 latency <500ms, error rate <0.1%. Implement CloudWatch alarms.

findings.title: Business Metrics — no custom metrics
findings.description: No custom metrics published. No CloudWatch put_metric_data, no business event tracking.
findings.gap: No business metrics. No visibility into quotes generated, rate lookups, or usage patterns.
findings.recommendation: Publish custom CloudWatch metrics: quote_requests_total, rate_lookups_total, quote_amount_average.

findings.title: Anomaly Detection and Alerting — no alerting
findings.description: No alerting configured. No CloudWatch alarms, no anomaly detection, no incident notification integration.
findings.gap: No alerting. Service failures go undetected until consumers report issues.
findings.recommendation: Implement CloudWatch alarms for 5xx rate, p99 latency, pod restarts, MongoDB connection failures. Enable anomaly detection.

findings.title: Deployment Strategy — basic rolling update
findings.description: K8s Deployment with 2 replicas uses default RollingUpdate strategy with TCP health probes. No canary, blue/green, or traffic shifting.
findings.gap: Rolling only. No ability to test with subset of traffic. No automated rollback on error rate increase.
findings.recommendation: Implement canary deployments via Argo Rollouts or App Mesh with progressive traffic shifting and automated rollback.

findings.title: Integration Testing — no tests
findings.description: No automated tests of any kind. README states 'No tests; no linting.' No test files, no test framework, no test scripts.
findings.gap: Complete absence of automated testing. Any change risks silent regression.
findings.recommendation: Add Jest/Mocha for unit tests, Supertest for API tests, testcontainers for MongoDB integration testing.

findings.title: Incident Response Automation — no runbooks
findings.description: No runbooks, no incident response automation, no self-healing patterns. Incident response is entirely ad hoc.
findings.gap: No runbooks or procedures. Response to incidents is undocumented and manual.
findings.recommendation: Create runbooks for MongoDB connection failure, high error rate, pod crash loops. Consider Lambda-based auto-remediation.

findings.title: Observability Ownership — no ownership defined
findings.description: No observability ownership. No CODEOWNERS, no dashboards, no named alarm owners, no team attribution.
findings.gap: No dashboards, no alarm owners, no team accountability for service health.
findings.recommendation: Define CODEOWNERS. Create CloudWatch dashboard. Assign alarm notification targets.
